name: Huang Tingting
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of YBM (Yaobangmang/药帮忙), the B2B pharmaceutical procurement platform run by Wuhan Xiaoyaoyao Pharmaceutical Technology (founded Dec 2015). Public sources found name Peng Yi (彭裔) as founder and Li Meng (李萌) as founder/CEO; no source tying a Huang Tingting to the company was found.
notes: Could not confirm identity. Searches for 'Huang Tingting' mostly return an unrelated SNH48 idol singer. Company sources: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1679729594749704 and https://finance.ifeng.com/c/87KuE7F91Ne. Verify via Hurun or company registry before outreach.

name: Joel Pobeda
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (former COO); no current public title confirmed
profile: French entrepreneur and one of four co-founders of Ledger, the Paris-based crypto hardware-wallet maker, alongside Eric Larchevêque, Thomas France and Nicolas Bacca. He served as COO in Ledger's early years, helping build its operations. His current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Ledger was formed in 2014 by merging his startup Chronocoin with BTChip and Eric Larchevêque's La Maison du Bitcoin.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ledger he founded Chronocoin, which let people buy Bitcoin with 3D-Secure credit/debit cards; its purchasing service was later rebranded Coinhouse, now one of France's main crypto brokerages.
notes: Very low public profile; sources are mostly profile aggregators. Alive status assumed (no death reports found). Best route likely via Ledger press/comms or LinkedIn.

name: Martin Tolar
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Alzheon Inc. (Framingham, MA)
profile: Czech-born neurologist and neuroscientist who founded Alzheon in 2013 to develop ALZ-801, an oral tramiprosate-prodrug anti-amyloid Alzheimer's drug licensed from Bellus Health. Before that he was Yale neurology faculty, worked in business development at Pfizer, and ran CoMentis, NormOxys and Knome. He also founded Tolion Health, an AI brain-health company.
interesting_fact: He received his M.D. from Charles University in Prague, did a Ph.D. on apolipoprotein E in Alzheimer's, and was on The Medicine Maker's Power List 2016-2019.
deep_cut_fact: As a medical student in Prague he helped organize and lead the November 1989 Velvet Revolution that ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia; he later received the Czech Laurels Award (2021).
notes: Company email is a general corporate inbox, not a personal one. He sits on the CERGE-EI Foundation board, another possible warm route.

name: Gil Geron
profile: Israeli cybersecurity executive who co-founded Orca Security in 2019 with Avi Shua, serving as chief product officer before becoming CEO in 2023. Orca pioneered agentless cloud security (its patented SideScanning approach). Before Orca he spent nearly 11 years at Check Point.
interesting_fact: Orca was co-founded by a group of senior Check Point veterans; Geron was promoted from CPO to CEO in 2023 to drive 'efficient growth'.
deep_cut_fact: His last role at Check Point (2017-2019) was overseeing its cybersecurity gateway and cloud products, capping nearly 11 years at the company before he left to start Orca.
notes: Frequent conference and podcast guest on cloud/AI security; reachable via Orca comms.

name: Brett Seyler
current_role: Co-founder, Forte; chairman of First Foundry (per Crunchbase)
profile: Games-industry technologist and investor who co-founded Forte (c. 2018-19), a platform helping game developers add blockchain economies, with former Kabam CEO Kevin Chou. He was earlier VP of Strategy and then GM of the Union division at Unity, after running the Torque engine business at GarageGames. Recent ventures include First Foundry and a stealth startup.
interesting_fact: Unity hired him from GarageGames in January 2010 as VP of Strategy, and he later led Unity's Union division bringing games to new platforms.
deep_cut_fact: He has a B.S. in Math from the University of Oregon and did graduate work in math, political science and economics; he joined GarageGames when it had about two dozen staff, before IAC bought a majority stake.
notes: Titles and dates vary across profiles; confirm current role (Forte vs First Foundry) on LinkedIn.

name: Court Cunningham
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Orchard (real estate tech, New York)
profile: Serial operator who ran local-marketing firm Yodle as CEO from 2007, growing it to $200M+ revenue before its 2016 sale to Web.com for $342M. In 2017 he co-founded Orchard, which lets homeowners buy a new home before selling the old one, and has expanded it across multiple US states. Former DoubleClick VP and Harvard MBA.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Yodle went from about $1M to over $200M in revenue and sold to Web.com for $342M.
deep_cut_fact: In high school he spent about three years building an 18th-century-style mahogany desk; when his woodworking teacher said the dividers were too loose, he made him start over ('You're better than good enough'). His mom's mantra was 'Action TNT' (today, not tomorrow).
notes: Regular Inman speaker; approachable via Orchard press.

name: John Schwarz
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman (former CEO), Visier Inc.
profile: Canadian-born software veteran (b. 1950) who spent ~25 years at IBM, was president/COO of Symantec, then CEO of Business Objects, which he sold to SAP in 2008, joining SAP's executive board. In 2010 he co-founded people-analytics company Visier in Vancouver with Ryan Wong and his sons Jan and Brett. Has sat on boards including Synopsys and Teradata.
interesting_fact: As CEO of Business Objects he doubled revenue to over $1.5B, made seven acquisitions and negotiated its sale to SAP.
deep_cut_fact: He holds both a BA in political science and a BSc in computer science from the University of Manitoba, plus an executive MBA from the University of Toronto; Dalhousie gave him an honorary law doctorate in 2004.
notes: Ryan Wong is now Visier CEO; Schwarz's title is variously given as chairman/founder. Visier co-founded with his sons - do not contact family.

name: Brandon Y Jeon
profile: Korean co-founder of Sendbird, the in-app chat, voice and AI-agent API company founded in 2013 with John S. Kim, Harry Kim and Forest Lee; it became a Korean-founded unicorn in 2021 (~$1B+ valuation). Profiles list him in developer-experience/quality-engineering and trust-and-safety roles at the company.
interesting_fact: Sendbird was named among Korea's new unicorns after its 2021 raise, with Jeon listed as one of its four co-founders.
notes: Very low public profile; titles differ across aggregators. Sendbird reportedly grew out of an earlier Korean community app (SmileMom) but only aggregator sources say so. Best route is via Sendbird or CEO John Kim.

name: Robbie Ferguson
profile: Australian entrepreneur who co-founded Immutable (originally Fuel Games, 2018) with brother James and Alex Connolly; it became a leading web3 gaming platform (Immutable X/zkEVM) valued at ~$2B+ (Hurun). Became the youngest person on the AFR Rich List at 25. Previously worked at KPMG Australia.
interesting_fact: In 2017-18 the brothers built Etherbots, billed as the world's first multiplayer competitive blockchain game, which brought in $1M in its first week.
deep_cut_fact: He finished top of his school, then started a computer science/law double degree at the University of Sydney (unfinished), where he met Immutable CTO Alex Connolly; he and James spent 'countless hours' on RuneScape and League of Legends as kids.
notes: Very active public speaker and on X/podcasts on web3 gaming; verify his X handle from Immutable's site before use.

name: Kevin Ho
current_role: Co-founder of Optimism; product team at OP Labs
profile: Co-founder of Optimism, the Ethereum layer-2 scaling network that grew out of the Plasma Group research team (2019). At OP Labs he works on product and oversees protocol development, contributing to the Optimism Collective and the OP Stack/Superchain used by chains such as Base.
interesting_fact: Optimism's founding team came out of Plasma Group, whose researchers devised the optimistic-rollup design while trying to make Plasma support apps like Uniswap.
deep_cut_fact: Before Optimism he was a 'hacker' at Cryptoeconomics.study (2018-19); he studied Computer Science with a Digital Media Design focus at the University of Pennsylvania.
notes: Low-profile builder; deep-cut source is a wiki-style aggregator, verify on LinkedIn. Bio confirmed by Blockworks author page.

name: John Tenet
current_role: Co-founder & CEO (sometimes Co-CEO), CHAOS Industries; co-founder of Epirus
profile: Defense-tech founder and investor who co-founded Epirus (2018), maker of Leonidas high-power-microwave counter-drone systems, then in 2022 co-founded CHAOS Industries, which builds radar/communications for national security. Formerly a partner at 8VC and principal at Valar Ventures.
interesting_fact: CHAOS Industries, his second defense startup, raised a $510M Series D at a reported $4.5B valuation, after a $275M Series C in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: CHAOS's founding team mixes Epirus and 8VC alumni (Tenet, Bo Marr) with a Palantir/UK Secret Intelligence Service veteran (Gavin Hood) and Brett Cummings of 8VC/Formation 8.
notes: Now primarily associated with CHAOS Industries rather than Epirus. Titles vary (CEO / Co-CEO).

name: David Coppins
profile: Boston-area entrepreneur who co-founded IntelyCare in 2016 with Ike Nnah and Chris Caulfield, building an app-based per-diem nurse staffing platform for post-acute care that reached unicorn status. Earlier he co-founded college-savings rewards company Upromise (1999) and was president of Virgin Pulse. Reported to have moved to executive chairman in 2023.
interesting_fact: He and his IntelyCare co-founders were named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2022 New England award winners.
deep_cut_fact: Long before healthcare, he co-founded Upromise in 1999, the program that turned everyday purchases into college-savings rebates, and later served as president of Virgin Pulse, part of Richard Branson's Virgin Group.
notes: Executive-chairman transition comes from a secondary source; confirm before outreach. Has written columns for MedCity News (https://medcitynews.com/author/dcoppins/).

name: Anna Sainsbury
profile: Vancouver entrepreneur who co-founded GeoComply in 2011 with David Briggs; its geolocation compliance tech underpins most legal US online gambling and is also used for streaming and fraud prevention. She was CEO 2011-2018, then chair, and returned as CEO in 2021. Previously Commercial Director at gaming testing firm TST.
interesting_fact: The company's origin traces to a 2009 gambling-industry conference in Macau, where she met her future co-founder.
deep_cut_fact: Her first job was at a coffee shop in West Vancouver, which she says taught her customer service; she is dyslexic and leans on verbal communication, and says yoga 'keeps me centered every day.'
notes: Confirm current title (CEO vs chair) on GeoComply site. Do not reference co-founder relationship details beyond the business.

name: Brian Murphy
profile: Florida State accounting/finance graduate and former PwC consultant who founded cybersecurity firm ReliaQuest in Tampa in 2007. It grew into an AI-driven security-operations (GreyMatter) company valued at about $3.4B. He is also an FSU trustee and active in Tampa's startup scene.
interesting_fact: He bootstrapped ReliaQuest with a second mortgage and credit cards and taught himself programming despite having no tech background.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the board of Embarc Collective, the Tampa nonprofit startup hub, giving back to the local founder ecosystem.
notes: Strong Florida/FSU ties (trustee). Possible warm routes via Embarc Collective or FSU.

name: Chris Pento
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Clear Street; executive & partner at White Bay (Uriel Cohen's family office)
profile: Wall Street operations veteran with 30+ years in financial services who co-founded cloud-native prime broker Clear Street in 2018 with Sachin Kumar and Uriel Cohen and built it to a multibillion-dollar valuation as CEO. He stepped down as CEO at the end of 2024 (succeeded by ex-Cboe CEO Ed Tilly) and joined investor White Bay.
interesting_fact: Clear Street rebuilt prime-brokerage clearing infrastructure from scratch in the cloud; he grew it into a $2.1B enterprise before handing the CEO role to former Cboe chief Ed Tilly.
deep_cut_fact: Before Clear Street he ran client services and operations at Knight Capital Group and was a managing director at Exos Financial; he studied at Rutgers University.
notes: Did an in-depth Fintech Leaders Substack interview: https://fintechleaders.substack.com/p/chris-pento-clear-street-ceoco-founder

name: Wang Junchao
profile: Reported founder of HARMAY, the Chinese beauty retailer (Beijing Huamei Lexiang Technology) that started as an online cosmetics/sample shop and became known for warehouse-style stores designed by AIM Architecture; it raised ~$200M in Series C/D at a reported $1B+ valuation. English-language press quotes a 'Will Wang' as founder & CEO, possibly the same person.
interesting_fact: HARMAY's Beijing store took inspiration from wet markets, part of its industrial-style experiential retail concept.
notes: Only Seedtable (https://seedtable.com/companies/harmay) names 'Junchao Wang' as founder; founder keeps a very low profile. Confirm identity before outreach.

name: Wang Qisong
current_role: Founder/legal representative, Sangon Biotech (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (per business registry aggregator)
profile: Listed as founder and legal representative of Sangon Biotech (生工生物), a Shanghai life-science reagents and services company (DNA synthesis, sequencing, reagents) belonging to the BBI Life Sciences group; the Shanghai entity was registered in 2003.
notes: Only aggregator (36Kr pitchhub) confirms the link; several unrelated academics share the name. Very private; route via company.

name: Adam Back
profile: British cryptographer and cypherpunk (b. 1970, London) who invented Hashcash in 1997, the proof-of-work scheme later used in Bitcoin mining and cited in the Bitcoin whitepaper. He co-founded Blockstream in 2014, which builds Bitcoin infrastructure (Liquid sidechain, Jade wallet, mining). PhD in distributed systems from Exeter.
interesting_fact: He invented Hashcash (1997), the proof-of-work function at the heart of Bitcoin mining.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1990s anti-ITAR crypto-export protests, his 'RSA in 3 lines of Perl' signature was printed on a 'munitions' T-shirt that was technically illegal to export from the US. His first computer was a Sinclair ZX81.
notes: Very active on X (@adam3us). Avoid leading with the Satoshi speculation; he has denied it.

name: Neri Tollardo
profile: Italian-born banker who co-founded Mexican fintech Plata (credit cards, now a licensed bank) in 2022 with ex-Tinkoff colleagues Alexander Bro and Danil Anisimov. Before that he was VP of strategy and head of international IR at Tinkoff Bank and spent nearly a decade at Morgan Stanley as head of CEEMEA banks equity research. Plata hit a ~$5B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: Plata raised $405M in April 2026 at about a $5B valuation, one of the fastest-growing fintechs in Latin America.
deep_cut_fact: He studied International Economics at Bocconi in Milan and holds a master's from the London School of Economics; he obtained Mexican citizenship in 2025.
notes: Citizenship detail from El CEO interview: https://elceo.com/negocios/entrevista-banco-plata-los-primeros-1000-mdd-y-la-proxima-expansion/ . Spoke at Milken Global Investors Symposium Mexico City 2026.

name: Bradley Kam
profile: Atlanta-born serial entrepreneur who co-founded Unstoppable Domains in 2018 with Matthew Gould, selling blockchain-based web3 domain names (.crypto, .x etc.); Hurun lists it as a ~$1B unicorn. Earlier he was president/CEO of Y Combinator-backed referral-marketing company Talkable. He moved to a board role in late 2023 and has a newer venture, Real.Photos.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he co-founded and ran Talkable, a YC-backed company building refer-a-friend programs for e-commerce brands; he holds a BA in political science from Emory University.
notes: Current roles (board, Real.Photos) from aggregator village.ai; verify. Some past press coverage of the founders is sensitive; keep outreach business-focused.
